title: feat(ui): router machine kind shows the router options on the Milling tab
body:
## What changed
- A machine file can state `"kind": "router"`. The words "CNC router" and "routing" also work.
- `Kind::from_word` reads a router word as `Kind::Mill`. A router keeps every mill rule.
- The new `machine::is_router` reads the word as a router. A router is never inferred from the axes.
- The new `camcraft_app::router_offer` module has one list of router options: `SheetJob` and `CornerRelief`.
- A router offers all options. A machine that is not a router offers none. A project with no machine offers all.
- The Setups page "Sheet job" group reads the list.
- The corner relief rows on Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset read the list.
- A stated option stays shown on a mill. Nothing is hidden or deleted from a project.
- MCP `get_job` reports `setups[].router_options` from the same function.

- The refusal text for an unknown kind now names "router".
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2410-router-kind.md`.

## Cause
CamCraft had no router kind. A router file was a plain mill. So no page could show router options for a router only.

## Design note
The escalation comment found that a new `Kind::Router` variant changes about 33 exhaustive matches in 5 crates. Each match can change posted G-code or a check. This PR uses a router word that reads as a mill. No match changes. No golden moves.

New pins:
- `crates/app/tests/router_kind.rs`:
  - `router_word_reads_as_a_mill`
  - `shipped_routers_state_the_router_kind`
  - `router_offers_the_router_options_and_a_mill_none`

title: ci(release): site_only dispatch builds and deploys only the site
body:
## What changed

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: the existing `workflow_dispatch` gets a boolean input `site_only` (default `false`).
  - `linux`, `macos`, `windows` and `wasm` have `if: ${{ !inputs.site_only }}`. `aur`, `snap` and `flatpak` need `linux`, so they are skipped too.
  - `publish` stays tag-only. Its condition also has `!inputs.site_only`, so a `site_only` run never publishes.
  - `site` is not changed. It builds from the dispatched ref and reads the version from that tree's `Cargo.toml` (0.25.0 on `site/v0.25.0`). With `wasm` skipped, app/ is the "not part of this copy" page, as for a failed wasm build.
  - `pages` deploys on the tag path as before. It also deploys on a `site_only` dispatch, but only from a `site/*` branch.
- `xtask/tests/release_site_tests.rs`: the new test `site_only_dispatch_runs_only_site_and_pages` pins the triggers, the input and each job condition, `publish` included.
- `docs/decisions/3276-site-redeploy.md`: the decision, the dropped options and the owner action.

## Why it is safe

- No new trigger. The triggers are still the `vX.Y.0` tag push and `workflow_dispatch` (the test pins the list).
- No fork path. Only a collaborator can dispatch a workflow. All jobs are GitHub-hosted.
- `publish` is still tag-only and skips on `site_only`. A `site_only` run cannot make a release page.
- The tag path and the plain dispatch path keep their behaviour: `inputs.site_only` is empty on a push and `false` by default.
- A `site_only` dispatch from `main` builds the site as a check and does not deploy it.

## Test run

- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo test -p xtask --test release_site_tests`: 2 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --test release_site_tests -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The YAML parses (`yaml.safe_load`), and the job conditions read as above.
- The branch `site/v0.25.0` (site fixes at `3bc320a8c`) passes `python -m unittest discover -s site/tests`: 82 tests OK.

## The same release.yml goes on site/v0.25.0 before the dispatch

GitHub runs a dispatch with the workflow file of the dispatched ref. The tag's `release.yml` has no `site_only` input. Thus `site/v0.25.0` has the `release.yml` of this PR as one commit, `ci(release): site_only dispatch (from PR #3277)` (head `e41d7129f`). That file is byte-identical to the file at this PR's head `b05a95c39`. If this PR changes `release.yml` again, the same file goes on `site/v0.25.0` again before the dispatch.

## Not exercised

- No workflow ran. The dispatch is still owed:
  `gh workflow run release.yml --ref site/v0.25.0 -f site_only=true`
- Owner action first: the `github-pages` environment must permit the branch policy `site/*`. Without it, GitHub refuses the `pages` deploy of the dispatch.

Process change: yes

body:
This PR is partial. It fixes two of the three `known-fail #2849` pins. The third pin needs a maintainer decision.

## What changed

- `lead_ext::axis_reseat` keeps the ring start only when the first edge is exactly on X or Y, or when no edge is nearer an axis. Before, it kept the start for each first edge within `axis_tol` (1 degree).
- `descent_xy::plan_xy` tries the first-cut tangent first, as before. When no radius fits and the first pass is a ring that returns to its start, it tries the direction of the closing edge. It uses that direction only within 1e-3 rad of the first-cut tangent.
- The `known-fail #2849` markers of two `lead_approach` pins are removed. Their asserts do not change.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/2849-two-pins.md`.

This is the held work of `issue/2849-three-pins` (`bfc1dc03b`), taken onto the latest main and gated again.

## Cause

- Test 2: the solidcore mesh gives a first edge 0.93 degrees off X. That edge is inside the tolerance, so the start was kept. `entry_arc::true_arc` posts G18/G19 only for an exact axis edge, so the arc was posted as chords.
- Test 1: the arc tangent came from the fitted walk arc. The ring polyline that returns to the start was 0.6 micron off that tangent line. The ring behind the start then crossed the arc hull on both sides, at each radius.

## Tests

- Pins (red on unchanged code, green with the fix):
  - `lead_approach::an_axis_aligned_lead_start_posts_the_users_arc_entry_as_g18_or_g19`
  - `lead_approach::the_horizontal_arc_entry_on_the_users_pocket_verifies_silent`
- Unit pins: `lead_ext::reseat_tests` (2 tests), `descent_xy::closing_tests` (1 test).
- Mutations:
  - Old `lead_ext.rs`: the G18/G19 pin goes red. The other pins stay green.
  - Old `descent_xy.rs`: the horizontal arc pin goes red. The other pins stay green.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): green. Steps: motion lib, `motion:xy_arc_entry`, `app:area_open`, `app:lead_approach`.
- Also run and green:
  - motion: `vertical_arc_entry`, `refusal_ghost`, `one_descent`, `level_links`, `entry_arc_3d`, `entry_approach`, `entry_arc`, `blind_floor`, `center_cut_law`, `corner_arc_radius`.
  - app: `wall_arc_entry`, `top_plane_noise`, `solid_law_goldens`, `recorded_post_streams`, `level_links`, `contour_none_lead`, `arc_entry`, `golden_cl`, `contour_start_point`, `shoulder_adaptive`.
  - post: `vertical_arc_entry`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes.

- Test 3 (`shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`) keeps its marker. A ring order change fixes it, but it makes `corner_arc_radius::the_crossing_law_keeps_the_arc_turns_and_crosses_nowhere` red. The two pins want opposite wall orders on a holed area. The maintainer decides the law (see the issue and the decision record).

title: fix(kernel): preserve validated STEP edges when healing exceeds the gap limit
body:
### Change

If healing removes edges and the healed solid fails the 0.001 mm endpoint limit, the STEP importer checks the original solid. It keeps the original edges only if the source meets that limit and passes the existing integrity and measurement checks and Solidcore's full level 2 validation. The mesher still checks the requested chord tolerance.

The importer checks endpoint gaps before computing volume and area. It polls for cancellation before rebuilding the source, before level 2 validation and before integration. It integrates only the selected body. When the source exceeds the endpoint limit, the refusal gives the source gap, limit, input-record edge index, vertex coordinates, edge counts and healed gap.

### Results on the reported part

The patched kernel importer still refuses the Fusion heater block. The source endpoint gap is 0.007736 mm, above the 0.001 mm limit. The worst source endpoint is on input-record edge 647 (zero-based). Healing reduces the edge count from 999 to 998 and increases the maximum gap to 0.011573 mm. The reader does not expose original STEP entity IDs for edges. The input-record index and model-space vertex coordinates locate the measured endpoint.

Two runs per commit used the same macOS arm64 machine, compiler options, debug dependencies and private STEP file. The order was old, new, new, old. User CPU time for the complete import fell from 15.29–15.62 s on `7fd89ffe9` to 7.42–7.45 s on `a65a65671`. Elapsed time was 18.79–20.55 s and 8.87–8.95 s, respectively. Other builds were running on the host.

The normal import stops at the gap check. A separate diagnostic ran level 2 directly on the original 345-face solid. The check alone took 0.404 s and reported 11 findings. This single sample does not establish a false-refusal rate.

### Regression tests

- The synthetic box with a 0.0007 mm edge has a source gap of 0.0008 mm. Healing increases it to 0.001063 mm. Recovery preserves all 13 edges and the box meshes at a 0.005 mm chord target.
- The ordinary healed box keeps 12 edges and has no source-recovery note.
- A box with an excessive source gap reports the measured gap, the limit, the independently identified edge and vertex, and the healed gap.
- A source that meets the endpoint limit but fails full geometry validation is refused.

### Verification and limits

- The quick gate against `origin/main` passed all 15 steps and 114 tests on `a65a65671`. All-target kernel Clippy passed with warnings denied.
- A successful level 2 recovery through the normal importer has been exercised on the synthetic box. The cost and acceptance rate of recovery on other production models are unmeasured. The GUI and MCP were not rerun on this build. The release-mode heavy gate has not been run on this head.
- The fallback applies to STEP exchange. Solidcraft keeps its existing persisted-model import contract. A net loss of edges triggers the fallback. If healing removes an edge and adds another, the count can conceal the loss and the ordinary gap refusal still applies.

The issue stays open for the decision about viewing a model whose source exceeds machining tolerance.

Effort: high

Changelog: STEP import preserves validated short edges when healing would exceed the endpoint tolerance. An over-limit source refusal locates the worst endpoint and reports both measurements.

Refs #3252

title: fix(wire): allow sharp inside corners at the wire radius
body:
## What changed

- A Wire Contour has a new per-operation option: `sharp_corners`. The default is off.
- Off: the behaviour does not change. A sharp inside corner is refused by name, as before.
- On: the cover law accepts an uncut rest up to the kerf offset (wire radius + spark gap). A sharp inside corner of 60 degrees or more keeps no more than that.
- The worst accepted rest is a note on the path (`wire EDM: sharp inside corners stated - ...`).
- The post's wire verify line also says the note. It is not a refusal.
- A rest past the kerf offset is still refused. The message says that the option was on.
- The option is in these places:
  - the project file (`sharp_corners`, absent when off, so old files read unchanged);
  - the wire page, Geometry tab ("Sharp inside corners at the wire radius"), applied by `EditOperationParams`;
  - MCP `edit_operation`, through the params DTO (no new tool is necessary).
- The 4-axis cut does not read the option. It keeps its own `heal_tolerance`.

## Cause

The cover law in `motion::wire_edm::laws` had one rule: each profile point must be within the kerf offset of the wire path. A sharp inside corner always breaks that rule. The report's known-good Sodick program cuts a sharp 10 mm square, and the corner takes the wire radius.

## Tests

- `motion` lib `wire_edm::sharp_tests::a_sharp_square_die_is_cut_when_sharp_inside_corners_are_stated`: a sharp 10 mm square die with k = 0.162 mm. Off is refused with the issue's numbers (0.1620, 0.0671). On is cut, with the note and rest 0.0671. The wire corner stays k from both sides. A punch gets no note.
- `motion` lib `wire_edm::sharp_tests::an_inside_corner_past_the_wire_radius_stays_refused`: a 30-degree corner stays refused with the option on.
- `app` `wire_sharp_corners::a_sharp_square_die_is_cut_and_verified_with_its_corner_rest_as_a_note`: the command path, generation, the verify line, the project round trip, and undo.

title: fix(sim): judge a wire taper at the model's chord tolerance, refuse an undercut
body:
## What changed

- A constant-taper Wire Contour is judged under the model's chord tolerance. The tolerance is the importer's chord promise (0.005 mm). A model that records a coarser chord uses that chord. 4-axis cuts keep their stated tolerance (#1170).
- The report line and a gouge name "the model's chord tolerance" for such a cut. Stated tolerances keep the old words.
- A new undercut law (`sim/src/verify/wire/undercut.rs`) judges the last pass of a constant-taper cut. A move that cuts a drafted wall at one judged height must cut it at every height. If it stands off the wall past the tolerance at another height, the post is blocked with `wire undercut: the kerf of move N stands ... mm off the part ...`.
- The law skips a move on a vertical wall. A taper on a vertical wall is a stated relief, as in the #536 and #1164 fixtures.
- `WireJob` has a new field `taper_chord`. `WireFinding::Gouge` has a new field `chord`. `WireVerdict` has a new field `chord`. The test literals get `taper_chord: false`.

## Cause

The generator lays the tapered wire from the section at one height. The facets at the other heights stand off the true cone by up to their chord. title: feat(wire): export a selected Agie opening for zero-step inspection
body:
The DXF import and Wire Contour selection prerequisites merged in #3193 and #3205. This PR adds the native zero-step inspection export.

## Change

Use `camcraft-cli export-agie-inspection <project> <operation> <new-directory>` for a saved operation.

A user can create an unassigned wire inspection operation on the Post page and choose one placed, closed DXF chain and an internal start. The user can save the operation and export a native Classic Cut 2S ISO/SBR/SBL directory with zero working steps. The CLI and MCP use the same entry points.

The exporter preserves the nominal line and circular arc geometry. It checks the source selection, closure, winding, rounding, arc extrema, start disk and supported mounted machine axes. It refuses a changed or unsuitable selection and a destination that exists. An inspection work does not become a qualified machining operation.

This first setup uses 10 mm height, a 3 mm internal start and a 0.25 mm wire. The reference piece has unknown physical X/Y dimensions. Its controller fields store zero length and breadth. The receipt identifies the unverified fixture, erosion settings, physical Z and perpendicular controller lead. It describes the controller’s quality request separately from an assigned erosion process. The nominal setup does not promise a historical start seam, lead or cut sequence.

## Verification on the refreshed head

Commit `d982d452b` merges upstream main at `4e0c81964` into the contributor branch. The only manual resolution was the generated MCP reference. The compiled registry and the published reference list the same 119 tools. A trial merge with main at `6308a5db5` completed without conflicts.

The targeted author check passed 104 tests on this head. These covered post (6), MCP (3), desktop (3), application regressions (74) and geometry (18). Strict all-target Clippy passed for the four touched crates. The complete quick selector listed 1,048 steps. The author ran the targeted quick alternative.

The refreshed CLI imported an unchanged drawing, reopened the saved operations and exported two native jobs. All six files matched the controller-checked files byte for byte. Each receipt reported zero working steps. Repeat exports refused to overwrite either job.

The official heavy gate passed all 254 selected steps in 62.7 minutes on this revision. The command exited with status 0.

```sh
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 4e0c81964
```

## Earlier verification on `d13c5eed1`

Contributor head: `d13c5eed15251af0a903396c1d96bba298b644d0`. Parent: `2d0fa64841a1b42dbacb330f75f6bab61897da10`.

All eight scoped tests passed on this earlier head: two post tests, three MCP tests and three desktop tests. Strict all-target Clippy passed for geometry, post, app and UI. The independent synthetic export preserved every directed edge, arc center and resource link. It wrote one start, one work and zero steps. The checks include:

- `agie_inspection_accepts_listed_chain_and_checks_mounted_travel_in_the_wcs`

On this earlier revision, 252 of 253 heavy steps passed. The bulk release build failed to link two test binaries when the device ran out of space. The refreshed revision has its own gate run.

The desktop authoring and selection use a real undoable operation. The documented MCP reference was regenerated from the compiled CLI. The public selection returned by `list_features` can be passed directly to `create_agie_inspection`. A regression narrows the mount travel and reverses an axis. Each case refuses before file creation.

We used an offline VM running a copy of the actual Agie Classic Cut 2S control. The control opened native files produced by CAMCraft. We checked the program and ISO identities, nominal orientation, hole size and position, setup height, zero separation and zero working steps. title: feat(import): state the STEP length unit, and ask for it when the file has none
body: ## What changed A STEP model import states the length unit that the model was read in. A STEP file that states no length unit is never read in a guessed unit. - **Kernel** (`crates/kernel/src/step_assumed_unit.rs`, `solidcore_step.rs`, `solidcore_step_import.rs`): `read_step_assuming` and `import_step_model_assuming` take the caller's millimetres per unit. For a file whose contexts state no length unit, the unit is written into each representation context before the read. The tolerance, the edge-gap cap and the chord are then in the same unit as the geometry. A file that states its own unit keeps it. A stated size outside 0.001..=1000 mm is refused by name. - **Geometry** (`crates/geometry/src/step.rs`): `parse_open_assuming`. A file with no length unit and no caller unit is `StepError::MissingUnits`. `StepMesh` carries `length_units_mm` and `assumed_mm`. - **App**: - `ImportError::StepUnitsMissing`. - `ImportModel::within_in` and `from_bytes_in`, and the unit option on each import path: the file, the bytes, the sourced load and the cadmpeg conversion. - A unit for a file that is not STEP is refused by name before parsing, as a facet budget is. - The last import note names the unit: `length unit: in (stated by the file)`, `length unit: in (stated at import; the file states no length unit)`, or `... (stated by the file; the in stated at import is not used)`. - **MCP and script**: `import_model` takes `units` (`"mm"` or `"in"`). `cam.import` takes it as the fourth argument. `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts` are regenerated. - **UI**: a refused unitless import opens the **Length unit** modal (`egui_app/step_units_prompt.rs`), with the buttons Millimeters (mm), Inches (in) and Cancel. The answer goes through the command queue (`CommandKind::ResolveStepUnits`) and runs the same import again. The import that lands is one undoable command. Cancel and Escape import nothing. An import-as-fixture binding is kept for the second import. - **Docs**: `units-and-coordinates.md` (it said that a unitless STEP file "is kept as millimetres") and a new `troubleshooting.md` entry. The decision record is `docs/decisions/1874-step-length-units.md`. ## Screenshot The Length unit prompt for a STEP file that states no length unit (the status line under it says the same): ## Decisions (see the decision record) - The file's own unit wins over the caller's (the DXF import does the reverse, #1862). A STEP unit context is an exact statement of the CAD system. - The chosen unit is not recorded on the model. A linked-file re-import asks again. - Tool holders, fixtures and tool bodies from a unitless STEP file are refused by name, with no prompt. ## Pinning tests - `camcraft-kernel` `step_assumed_unit` (3): a unitless box reads 25.4² times the area in inches; the file's own unit wins; an out-of-range unit is refused by name. - `camcraft-app` `step_units_import` (5): the typed refusal; the inch and mm imports and their notes; the file's mm, in and m notes; a unit for an STL is refused; MCP `import_model` with no unit, a bad unit and `in`. - `camcraft-ui` lib `step_units_tests` (5): the question, the answer as one undoable import (inch is 25.4 times the mm width), Cancel, and no question for a file that states its unit. - `camcraft-ui` lib `egui_app::tests::step_units_prompt` (4): the labels, no prompt without a question, a unit button, Cancel and Escape. - Updated, because each STEP import now ends with the unit note: `import_step_outward` (3 tests) and `import_step_closed_shell` `a_flipped_face_is_named_in_the_import_result_and_the_mcp_answer`. They assert the unit note in place of "no notes". No assertion is weaker. ## Gates Final head b5637db2b (the review fixes on 2649bb17e), Windows x86_64, without sccache: - Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 1033 steps, 1032 ok. The one red step is `ai_guide_calls_match_live_tools_list`, the CRLF defect #3119, which this PR does not touch. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (kernel and geometry on 2649bb17e; they did not change after it). - Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`): `kernel heavy` (17 steps), `motion heavy` (37 steps) and `app heavy` (198 steps), after one release build. 253 steps ok, 0 failed, 26.1 min. The known-fail steps of #1950 and #2849 are red as expected. (The run on 2649bb17e also had 253 steps ok.) - Note: with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`, two gate runs here failed with "can't find crate" (`num_enum`, then `flecs_ecs`) and the warning `ignoring -C extra-filename flag due to -o flag`. The runs without sccache are correct. This is a local cache matter, not this change. ## Review fixes (b5637db2b) - `crates/app/tests/cadmpeg_import.rs`: the eight `load_open_within` calls in the `#[cfg(unix)]` module pass `None` for the new `units` argument. This module does not compile on Windows, so it is not in the Windows gates above. It needs a build on Linux or macOS. - `State::take_step_units`: each import start takes the chosen unit, whatever its file. A unit never waits for a later import of the same file. That path uses the same `parse_model_open_in`. - `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` and `crates/app/src/script/api.rs` were already over 400 lines. They grow by 2 and 7 lines. title: feat(catalog): a catalog case can expect a refusal
body:
Stacked on #3139 (merge #3139 first).

## What changed

- The `expect` field of `case.toml` takes `"post"` or `"refusal"`. Other values are refused by name.
- The 12 existing cases change to `expect = "post"`. #3139 held a free-text description there. The README of each case keeps that text.
- A refusal case has no `<case>.nc`. It has `refusal.txt`: the refusal lines that the script host records, one line each.
- The script of a refusal case saves the project, then runs the refused step without a catch. The script run ends with an error.
- The app tests `regenerates` and `rebuilds` read `expect`:
  - `regenerates` opens the saved project in the script host (`cam.load`, `cam.generate`, `cam.post`). It compares `ScriptOutcome::errors` with `refusal.txt`.
  - `rebuilds` runs `build.camscript` with `camcraft-cli`. It requires a failed exit, a saved project, no `.nc`, and the same lines on stderr.
  - The two tests also open the project and check that its model is embedded, with no file link.
- `cargo xtask catalog --check` accepts a refusal case without a `.nc` file. It runs the script and compares the refusal lines. A refusal case with a `.nc` file fails the layout check.
- `cargo xtask catalog` (rebuild) writes `refusal.txt` for a refusal case.
- New case `2d/drill-overfeed`: an 80 x 50 x 10 mm plate with two 6 mm holes. The Drill feeds at 400 mm/min, above the 115 mm/min of tool DR-0600. The post refuses it by the #2598 clause.
- The 2D operation guide lists the new case under Drill (generated block).
- The catalog README documents `expect` and `refusal.txt`.
- The script host law does not change.

Process change: yes
Effort: high. No escalation.

## Cause

The catalog tests and `--check` required a posted `.nc` for each case. A case could not show a refusal.

## Tests

New pins:

- `catalog_2d_drill_overfeed::regenerates`
- `catalog_2d_drill_overfeed::rebuilds`

2. `refusal.txt` says 120 mm/min in place of 115: the two case tests fail with `refusal lines differ from refusal.txt`. `cargo xtask catalog --check` fails with the want/got lines.
3. The refusal case posts (feed lowered to 115 in the script and the project): `regenerates` fails with `the post was not refused`; `rebuilds` fails with `build.camscript ended without an error`.
4. `xtask/src/catalog.rs` from #3139: `catalog_check_verifies_refusal_case` fails with `missing drill-overfeed.nc`.
5. The `expect` value guard removed: `catalog_expect_takes_post_or_refusal_only` fails.

title: feat(ui): load machine and post files from the user's disk in the browser
body:
## What changed

The browser build now loads the user's own machine (`.mch`) and post (`.cps`) files. The bytes come from the browser, not from a path.

- **Load machine (.mch)** and **Load post (.cps)** are live in the browser. They open the browser file picker. A picked machine is mounted. A picked post is selected.
- The Machine page has a new button **Load folder (.mch, .cps)** in the browser build only. It opens `<input webkitdirectory multiple>`. It adds each `.mch` and `.cps` file of the folder to the session lists. It does not need the File System Access API.
- A drop with a `.mch` or `.cps` file goes to a new module `setup_file_drop`. One file is mounted or selected. Several files only join the lists. One status line counts the files that landed and names each refused file with its reason.
- On the desktop, one dropped `.mch` or `.cps` on disk goes to `LoadMachineFile` or `SelectPostFile` by its full path.
- A new app module `session_files` keeps each file by its bare name for the session, on the thread that loaded it. A file enters it only when it passes the checks of a file from disk: a machine must validate and parse, a post must compile and run.
- The readers of machine and post files consult the session store first, then the disk. So `LoadMachineFile`, `SelectPostFile` and the MCP tools run unchanged. Each mount and post choice stays one undo step.
- Session machines show in the machine catalogue (`library::enumerate`). Session posts show in the post combo list.
- A saved project that names a session file which is not loaded again is refused by that name (#2319). There is no fallback.

## Cause

The browser build had no disk and no picker for these files. `browser_files::refusal` greyed Load machine and Load post with `NEEDS_PICKER`. The file drop took model files only. The readers of `PostRef::File` and the machine file read only from disk.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/browser_setup_files.rs`:

- `a_dropped_mch_mounts_by_its_name_and_one_undo_takes_it_away`
- `a_dropped_cps_is_selected_and_posts_from_its_bytes`
- `several_dropped_files_land_and_each_bad_one_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_malformed_pick_is_refused_by_name_and_changes_nothing`
- `a_picked_folder_fills_both_lists_and_a_picked_file_mounts_or_selects`
- `the_machine_and_post_load_buttons_are_live_in_the_browser` (AccessKit label, role `Button`, enabled state for "Load machine (.mch)", "Load folder (.mch, .cps)" and "Load post (.cps)"; no folder button on the desktop)

Other tests:

- `session_files::tests::a_bad_file_is_refused_by_name_and_never_kept` (app unit test; also pins the refusal by name for a project that names a file that is not loaded).
- `setup_file_drop::tests::one_file_is_for_its_own_kind_in_any_case`.
- Updated for the new law: `browser_files::tests::every_picker_and_folder_command_is_refused_by_name_in_the_browser`, `a_picker_the_browser_lacks_is_refused_by_name_not_ignored`, `a_file_button_is_greyed_with_its_reason_in_the_browser`.

Red before the fix (reduced pins on unchanged `upstream/main`):

- the drop pins failed with `drop refused: drop-2950-vmc.mch is not a model file (read: .stl, .obj, .step, .stp, .sc, .solidcraft)`;
- the button pin failed with `LoadMachineDialog runs the browser's picker` / `left: Some("Not available in the browser yet: ...")`.

Mutation checks (old code put back, pins run, code restored):

- `crates/ui/src/browser_files.rs` from upstream: `the_machine_and_post_load_buttons_are_live_in_the_browser` red.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs` from upstream (drop route not called): the three drop pins red.
- `crates/app/src/posting.rs` from upstream (no session read at post time): `a_dropped_cps_is_selected_and_posts_from_its_bytes` red.
- `session_files::add_post` without its compile check: `several_dropped_files_land_and_each_bad_one_is_refused_by_name` red.
- All pins green again after each restore.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ran all 428 steps on the previous head. 427 passed. `ui suites: lib` failed in three machines-pane tests. The cause was a process-global store: the session machines of the new tests leaked into the machine list of tests on other threads.
- The fix makes the store thread-local. The browser runs on one thread.
- On the final head, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only "app suites: lib" --only "ui suites: lib"` is green (ui lib 1385 passed, 0 failed). Only `crates/app/src/session_files.rs` changed between the two heads, plus one test comment and the decision file. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Goldens moved

- The wasm32 build. The `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target is not installed on this machine, so the wasm-only code was not compiled. That code is: the folder input and batch read in `file_pick.rs`, the async drop read in `setup_file_drop.rs`, and the dialog openers in `state_picked.rs`. A reviewer with the target must run `cargo check -p camcraft-ui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

title: feat(tools,app): cutting data for wood, MDF, plywood, acrylic and HDPE
body:
## What changed

- The cutting table has six new work materials: `softwood`, `hardwood`, `mdf`, `plywood`, `acrylic` and `hdpe`.
- Each new row has a cutting-speed window and a 10 mm chip load for HSS and carbide. Each row also has Kienzle constants.
- The new rows are appended. The table is indexed in `WorkMaterial::ALL` order. A project file stores the word, so old files read the same.
- New module `crates/tools/src/cutting_router.rs` gives the router chip load by cutter diameter. The points are 3 mm 0.30, 6 mm 0.65, 10 mm 1.0 and 12 mm 1.15 of the 10 mm chip load. Below 3 mm the scale falls in proportion to the diameter. Above 12 mm it holds.
- `WorkMaterial::chip_scale(d)` selects the router curve for a router material. It selects the existing metal bands (`fz_scale`) for the other materials.
- `app::cutting::compute` uses `chip_scale`. On a router material, a V-bit (`ToolKind::Taper`) reads its chip load at half its diameter.
- The turning table has the same six rows, because it is also indexed in `ALL` order.
- The `camcraft-tools speeds` command, the MCP tool descriptions, the generated `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the `camcraft-mcp` skill list the new words.

The rpm clamp is the existing code in `compute`. It clamps to `spindle_min` and `spindle_max`. It then calculates the feed again at the clamped rpm, so the chip load stays the same. It names each clamp in `notes`. This PR does not change that code. The new tests pin it for a router spindle.

## Cause

The table had only aluminium, steels, cast iron, brass and POM. A router user who cut wood or plastics got no suggestion, or a suggestion from a metal row. The metal bands also give each cutter from 3 to 6 mm the same chip load. For wood, that is approximately two times too much for a 1/8 in cutter.

## Tests

New suite `crates/app/tests/cutting_router.rs`:

- `router_materials_have_words_and_round_trip`
- `each_router_material_matches_the_hand_calculation_on_a_6mm_end_mill`: S and F for each material against a hand calculation.
- `end_mill_v_bit_and_ball_nose_stay_inside_a_router_spindle`: end mills of 3, 6 and 12 mm, a V-bit and a ball nose, for each material and tool material, on a 10000-24000 rpm spindle.
- `a_v_bit_reads_its_chip_load_at_half_its_diameter`
- `a_router_spindle_clamps_both_ways_and_keeps_the_chip_load`: 3 mm softwood is held at 24000 rpm, with F 4320. 12 mm HSS acrylic is raised to 10000 rpm, with F 2875. Each clamp is named.

Unit tests in `crates/tools/src/cutting_router.rs` pin the curve points, the ends and that the curve never falls.

Before the fix, the suite did not compile: the materials did not exist.

title: feat(2d): V-Carve operation - depth from the region width along the medial axis
body:
## What changed

- A new 2D operation, **V-Carve** (kind tag 45). A V-bit carves a closed region. The tip follows the medial axis. At each point the depth is where the cone touches the two walls. A maximum depth (`Top Z - Bottom Z`) limits the cut.
- Motion kernel: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/vcarve.rs`, `vcarve_axis.rs`, `vcarve_walk.rs`.
  - The tip positions come from the largest inscribed circle at each sampled boundary point. The centre of that circle is a point of the medial axis.
  - The cone keeps a wall allowance of 0.01 mm. The kernel checks each straight feed move against the outline before it writes the move. A move that fails becomes a retract and a new plunge.
  - A branch into a corner that turns less than 20 degrees is not ridden. A tessellated circle is one dip, not a star.
  - Deep carves step down. An optional flat-clearing pass uses offset rings of the same V-bit inside the wall pass.
  - The cone height also limits the depth. The path carries a note when it does.
- App: the `VCarve` kind row, the generator arm, the seed, heights, the mark depth law (`DepthLaw::Mark`), the project-file arm `VCarve` (appended, no version step), posting and the setup sheet.
- Sim: a new `Mode::Carve`. It has the stand-downs of `Mode::Engrave`, and the crossing law is off. The walk rides each axis branch from its two walls, so the two rides lie on one another by design.
- UI: a V-Carve parameter page and an original icon (`assets/ui/op-v-carve.png`, `.svg`).
- MCP: the generic `add_operation` tool takes the kind `V-Carve`. `list_operation_types` lists the kind and its fields. No new MCP tool is necessary.
- The V-bit is the existing `Taper` tool kind. The included angle is the tool's `tip_angle`.
- Review correction: generation, stock simulation and the live check before posting use `min(Top Z - Bottom Z, cone height)` for the V-Carve mark budget. Other marks keep their radius limit. A legal 60-degree V-bit cut can exceed the bit radius.
- Latest review correction: the live check uses `cutter_depth_limit(&job.params, &job.tool)`. A legal deep stock-source carve now has the same mark budget at generation, simulation and posting.
- Merge of main: Slot Undercut keeps its declaration, row and tag at 44. V-Carve appends at 45. Both operations keep their verification exemptions.

## Sources (literature)

The algorithm is written from these published sources. The module heads name them.

- H. Blum, "A transformation for extracting new descriptors of shape", 1967 (the medial axis transform).
- H. I. Choi, S. W. Choi, H. P. Moon, "Mathematical theory of medial axis transform", Pacific J. Math., 1997.
- J. Ma, S. W. Bae, S. Choi, "3D medial axis point approximation using nearest neighbors and the normal field", The Visual Computer, 2012 (the tangent-circle shrink).
- M. Foskey, M. C. Lin, D. Manocha, "Efficient computation of a simplified medial axis", 2003 (the separation angle).
- M. Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", 1991 (the floor rings).
- The cone law `depth = radius / tan(angle / 2)` is machine-tool handbook geometry.

The session had no web access, so no Perplexity search ran. camlib was a feature list only. No code or output of another program was read.

## Cause

There was no V-carve operation. The engrave ride follows a line at one depth only.

## Tests

- `crates/motion/tests/v_carve.rs` (11 tests):
  - `the_cone_never_leaves_the_region`: sweeps the cone along the path against the region outline.
  - `the_depth_follows_the_width_of_the_region`, `a_sharp_corner_rises_to_the_surface`, `a_stroke_is_cut_in_one_engagement`, `a_tessellated_circle_is_one_dip_not_a_star`, `the_maximum_depth_limits_the_cut`, `flat_clearing_removes_the_floor_the_cone_cannot_reach`, `a_deep_carve_steps_down`, `a_cone_shorter_than_the_maximum_depth_limits_the_cut_and_says_so`.
  - `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`: angle, diameter, maximum depth, stepdown, feed, clearance, retract, stepover, non-finite numbers, an empty region.
  - `degenerate_regions_give_a_clean_answer`: a fuzz set of 45 regions (zero width, a 1 micron sliver, a bow tie, a spike, far from the origin, 40 seeded random polygons), with and without flat clearing. Each gives a clean error or a path whose cone stays inside.
- `crates/app/tests/v_carve_op.rs` (9 tests):
  - `a_sixty_degree_carve_deeper_than_the_bit_radius_is_legal`: a 10 mm, 60-degree V-bit cuts 6 mm deep in a 20 mm square. Generation has no blocking warning. Stock simulation has zero gouge cells. The program posts.

title: fix(slot): cut the round ends of a slot wider than the tool
body:
## What changed

- A Slot wider than its tool now runs one wall lap at each level, after the rows.
- The lap follows the boundary of the tool centre stadium: two straight sides and two half circles.
- Each half circle is a chain of arcs (G02/G03). The chain is split at every row end on it and at its tip, so no arc is more than 90 degrees.
- The rows and the lap compute a row end with one function (`cap_point`). Each row join meets the lap at the same point to the bit.
- The lap starts where the last row ends and closes at that point.
- Under `climb` the lap is counterclockwise (the slot's air on the left, the same sense as the rows). Under conventional it is clockwise.
- A full-width slot (`h = 0`, one row on the centre line) does not change.
- The lap code is in the new module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_lap.rs`. `slots.rs` is 394 lines.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2906-slot-round-ends.md`.

## Cause

A row touches a round end only at its end point. The move between two rows is a straight line. The tool did not follow the arc between two row ends. On a 10 mm slot with a 6 mm tool, 0.86 mm stayed on the wall of each round end.

## Why the arcs are split at the row ends

The first version used two quarter arcs for each cap. The quick gate refused it on 8 app suites. The verifier's crossing law (a) flattens an arc into chords inside its circle. A row join is a chord that ends exactly on the circle, so it crossed those flattened chords, and the post was held. With the split, the join and the lap share their vertices. The law reads a shared vertex as a touch, not a crossing. The crossing law does not change.

## Tests

- New pin: `crates/motion/tests/slot_round_ends.rs`
  - `wide_slot_cuts_its_round_ends_climb`
  - `wide_slot_cuts_its_round_ends_conventional`
  - `wide_slot_with_rows_off_the_tips_cuts_its_round_ends`
  - Each point on the stadium wall must be within the tool radius of the tool centre path (limit 0.01 mm). No tool centre point may leave the cutter centre stadium. `crossed_pairs` (the verifier's crossing law) must be empty.
  - Red before the fix: `climb=true z=9: 0.855 mm left on the wall at (28.536, 18.536)`.
- New unit tests in `slot_lap.rs`: the lap closes on its start; each row end is a lap vertex; CCW from `b` runs the +n side first; CW from `b` turns round `b` first.
- Mutations repeated on head `35020f6cc294c3b6266be720b3c9d2b178c970f9`:
  - Disable the wall lap: all three `slot_round_ends` tests fail. The climb and conventional tests leave 0.855 mm on the wall. Restore the source: all three tests pass.
  - Remove the row-end splits: `wide_slot_with_rows_off_the_tips_cuts_its_round_ends` fails its crossing assertion. Restore the source: all three tests pass.
  - Both restorations match the reviewed source byte for byte. The worktree has no source changes.
- Expected-change test updates:
  - `crates/motion/tests/machining2d.rs`: `slot_offsets_rows_across_a_wide_channel`, `conventional_slot_starts_at_the_far_end`, `slot_stock_to_leave_narrows_the_center_area` read the rows as the prefix of the level and pin the lap (arc count, direction, tips at x = -7 and 47, close at the last row end). `slot_helix_orbits_in_the_certified_channel` counts only descending arcs as the helix.
  - `crates/app/tests/operations.rs` (`an_entry_edit_marks_the_slot_stale_and_the_orbit_proves_itself`): an orbit is a descending arc. The planar arcs are the lap.
  - `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/case_2d_slots.rs`: the Slot now has 8 arc blocks (4 for each level).
  - `crates/app/tests/clearance_in_stock.rs` (`a_slot_traverse_at_a_clearance_plane_inside_the_stock_is_convicted_and_holds_the_post`): see "Side effect" below.

## Final-head validation

Head: `35020f6cc294c3b6266be720b3c9d2b178c970f9`. No new commit was needed for this validation request.

Base: `upstream/main` at `a35c9cb8197f484fca0f8311610bdc8594111a0f`. The diff merge base is `11402dba4c849c5f827dccebc14f850196614311`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 732 steps; 731 pass and one fails its time limit.
- The failed test is `adaptive_troch_parallel::wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes`. It takes 123.369 seconds against a 90-second debug limit. No geometry assertion fails.
- The isolated failed-step retry uses `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=1`. Its one gate step passes; both tests pass. The suite takes 107 seconds.
- The CL and post fixture readers pass. The changed golden readers pass.
- Motion library tests: 494 pass, 10 ignored. The three `slot_round_ends` pins pass.
- App `operations`: 121 pass, 6 ignored. App `example_catalog`: 33 pass, 2 ignored.
- App `clearance_in_stock` and `solid_law_goldens` pass.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: exit 0. All 235 steps complete in 109.1 minutes, with zero unexpected failures. Both reached lanes, motion and app, run in full.
- Reached motion lane: 37 steps, 57 tests pass, 2 expected failures reproduce.
- Reached app lane: 197 steps, 43 tests pass, 4 expected failures reproduce. The shared build is the remaining step.
- Six known-fail tests produce their expected red results. The gate accepts these expected results.
- Motion heavy library tests: 8 pass. Motion `finish3d`: 33 pass.
- App heavy `operations`: 6 pass. App `rotary_field_parity`: 6 pass in 864.35 seconds.
- App `shared_face_bodies_finish`: 6 pass in 2268.32 seconds.

Expected failures:

- `motion heavy: known fail #1950 the_stock_ring_level_reaches_the_air_planner_with_the_stock`
- `motion heavy: known fail #1950 the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note`
- `app heavy: known fail #2849 an_axis_aligned_lead_start_posts_the_users_arc_entry_as_g18_or_g19`
- `app heavy: known fail #2849 the_horizontal_arc_entry_on_the_users_pocket_verifies_silent`
- `app heavy: known fail #1950 the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level`
- `app heavy: known fail #2849 fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`

- `env -u RUSTC_WRAPPER -u RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 cargo clippy -j 8 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0 in 4 minutes 8 seconds.
- The final worktree is clean. No golden file changes remain. The head is unchanged.

## Side effect (please check in review)

In `clearance_in_stock`, the slot's lateral traverse between its levels was convicted only because the uncut crescents of the round ends stood in its path. The traverse stays inside the slot's own channel. With the ends cut, the verifier acquits it. The plane is still convicted by the first traverse (`FirstTraverseLow`, #2901) and by the rapid from the plane down into the stock (`RapidInStock { at: 1 }`). The post is still held with "travels through stock". The test now asserts these facts.

## Goldens moved

title: fix(kernel): measure a fan at a spline pole by its true sag
body:
## Problem and change

A closed STEP solid can have a spline face that ends at a pole. The old deviation measure can reject its valid mesh.

`mesh_pole::settle` moves the free parameter at a pole to the mean of the other two triangle corners. It uses one side of the period. It keeps the move only when the surface point stays within 1e-9 mm. `mesh_deviation::face` applies this step before it samples a spline triangle. Analytic faces keep their existing path. The deviation bounds do not change.

The PR includes two original fixtures:

- `testdata/models/sphere_quarter_pole.step`: a quarter sphere, R 25, with a rational B-spline dome and an apex pole.
- `testdata/models/q02_3d_mold.step`: the recorded SolidCraft QA part from #3034. The file has 347101 bytes. SHA256: `111862a3c03262db764d92e63c5c32f384541b14840d494f6bf3bf4fc5bb9567`.

Both fixtures have STEP agreement rows and named tests. No HSMWorks source or assets were used.

## Cause and readings

The issue reports an open mesh on v0.24.0. On upstream/main `8be100737`, the import itself refused q02:

```text
solid #3738 'Mould' could not be tessellated: machining mesh: face Some(10) stands 5.089e-1 mm off its surface, tolerance 5e-3 mm
```

Face 10 is the ellipsoid boss (`#3666`), with a pole at its top. Its mesh sag is about 0.004 mm. The old measure interpolated the free parameter across half the period. Its projection hint was then on the far side of the surface. A finer chord did not reduce the measured bound.

With the fix, the recorded q02 file imports with 48780 facets and no open edges. Its signed volume is 97163.50 mm^3. SolidCraft reports 97165.69 mm^3. The test allows 10 mm^3.

The slice at z = 19.6875, the reported height, has area 1382.27 mm^2. Slices at z = 18.5, 20, 25 and 29 also close. The test checks the measured areas within 0.5 mm^2.

## Regression pins

- Kernel `mesh_deviation_pole::a_fan_at_a_spline_pole_measures_by_its_true_sag`.

- App `import_step_spline_pole::a_solid_with_a_spline_pole_imports_closed_and_slices`.

- App `import_step_q02_mold::the_recorded_q02_mould_generates_a_3d_flat_finish` (heavy lane).

The q02 generation pin uses the full recorded model and the normal undoable generation command. It uses Flat Finish3D, BN-0600, top z = 30 mm, bottom z = 18 mm, stepover 2 mm, and tolerance 0.05 mm. It checks finite moves and more than 10 mm of horizontal Feed on the base at z = 18 mm. The initial release run passed: 1 test, 8.27 s. The final-head heavy run also passed this pin: 1 test, 7.90 s.

Mutation check on this follow-up:

```text

```

Base: upstream/main `6e1805bfdae52fcfea71a946d381dfbfdefc79f5`.

title: fix(2d): read a drafted side as a wall, not as a modelled chamfer
body:
## What changed

- A no-pick 2D chamfer now reads a drafted side as a wall. It does not read it as a modelled chamfer.
- The chamfer takes a third section of the material, half way between the top plane and the corner plane.
- A piece of a top loop is a drafted wall when two conditions are true:
  - It stands off the wall by no more than `depth * tan(15 deg)`.
  - The corresponding half-depth wall covers the expected segment along the whole piece within `LEAN_SLACK` (0.0001 mm).
- A loop with drafted pieces and no bevelled piece rides its wall at the corner depth. It counts with the sharp loops (#2596). Thus a plate with no modelled chamfer breaks every edge, the drafted side and the pocket included.
- The half-depth loop matches the corner wall by winding and the smallest symmetric whole-loop vertex gap. Each piece requires full coverage by parallel segments with the same direction. Collinear section vertices are allowed.
- `partly_bevelled` becomes `read`, which returns a `Reading`. The #2887 refusal text does not change.
- `ride_loops` takes two new arguments: `mid` (the half-depth section) and `depth`. The one caller, `material_source.rs`, makes the half-depth section.

## Cause

PR #2894 refuses a loop that is bevelled on only part of its length. It reads each piece more than 0.05 mm off the wall as "bevelled". A drafted side also stands off the wall. With a 1 mm chamfer and a 90 degree cone, a draft of more than about 3 degrees is more than 0.05 mm off. The plate was refused with a "modelled chamfer" message.

Two sections cannot tell a draft from a small modelled chamfer. A third section checks the straight slope within the section grid slack. A draft puts the half-depth section at half the offset. A modelled chamfer that ends before the corner plane departs from this slope. The review found that a 25% residual allowance admitted a 0.25 mm bevel that ends at 0.7 mm depth. The check now uses `LEAN_SLACK` (0.0001 mm). A later review found that one matching midpoint or an unrelated hole could excuse a partial bevel. The check now requires continuous coverage on the corresponding wall along the whole piece.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride_tests.rs`:

- `a_plate_with_one_drafted_side_rides_its_wall`: #2887's plate with its X0 side drafted 3.5, 5 and 10 degrees. Red on unchanged code: `the edge loop near X0.087 Y20.000 carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length`.
- `a_small_bevel_on_one_side_is_no_draft`: a 0.2 mm modelled bevel on one side is still refused.
- `a_bevel_ending_below_half_depth_is_no_draft`: the review fixture has a 0.25 mm bevel that ends at 0.7 mm depth. The test requires the partial-bevel refusal for a 1 mm ride.
- `a_side_whose_slope_turns_back_is_no_draft`: a side that turns back at half depth is refused.
- `half_depth_must_match_along_the_whole_piece`: a slanted half-depth wall that matches only at the midpoint is refused.
- `an_unrelated_mid_depth_hole_must_not_excuse_a_bevel`: a buried hole cannot supply the outer wall match.
- `a_drafted_side_allows_collinear_half_depth_vertices`: a straight draft still passes with extra collinear section vertices.
- `a_straight_face_steeper_than_a_draft_is_a_chamfer`: a 45 degree bevel deeper than the ride is still refused.
- The #2887 tests (`a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_by_name`, `..._with_an_extra_vertex_too`) still pass. The old test calls go through a small `ride` helper.

Mutation checks (each guard taken out, then put back):

- Drafted reading off: `a_plate_with_one_drafted_side_rides_its_wall` red.
- Half-depth check off: `a_small_bevel_on_one_side_is_no_draft` red.
- Slope limit off: `a_straight_face_steeper_than_a_draft_is_a_chamfer` red.
- Drafted match arm after the vertex-gap arm: the 3.5 degree case of the drafted pin red (it rode the top loop, inside the part).

Verification on head `b582f0cf12ab38fa1d9f2d7a0c7d4be13db241c4`:

- Both new refusal pins fail with the prior head behavior restored (RED). Both pass with the fix restored (GREEN).
- All 21 `chamfer_ride` library tests pass, including the collinear positive pin.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. All 139 steps pass. Tests: 1943 passed, 0 failed, 64 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: GREEN. Both steps pass. Tests: 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN. All 235 steps pass in 38.2 minutes. Every reached motion and app target ran, with no manual skips. Tests: 57 motion and 43 app; 100 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored. Six expected-failure validations were verified: two motion and four app.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- No app-level test with a real drafted STEP or STL model. The pins use hand-built sections.
- A drafted side under a tilted frame. The check measures along the frame's lean, but no test covers it.

## Overlaps

PRs #3058, #2836 and #2714 touch `crates/app/src/operation/material_source.rs`. They change other match arms, not the `Chamfer2D` arm. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2929-chamfer-drafted-side.md`.

## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs`: before each ring after the first, the tool climbs straight up to clearance at the end of the last ring. Then the ring's ladder enters from clearance, as the first ring does. This applies to the flat mode and to the vault.

## Cause

Each ring runs its own level ladder (ring-major order). The first descent of a ladder expects the tool at clearance. After the first ring, the tool stood on that ring's floor. title: fix(ui): an undersize-hole warning no longer hides a shank avoid hit
body:
## What changed

- `fold_warnings_located` (`crates/ui/src/operations.rs`) groups `Warning::DrillUndersize` under key `223`. Before, it used `216`. That is the key of `Warning::AvoidHit` with `FixturePart::Shank` (the avoid range is `216..=220`).
- A group prints only the line of its first warning. When the undersize hole came first, the pane folded the blocking "Do not touch" shank hit into the advisory line as "repeated on 1 more move". The pane did not show the shank hit.
- `UndercutLift` (added on main by #1444, commit 5452810e5) groups under key `222`. Main gave it `217`, the key of `Warning::AvoidHit` with `FixturePart::Holder`: the same fault. The merge of main (9f1f7adb1) moves it.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3040-drill-undersize-fold-key.md`.

## Pinning test

`operations::warning_fold_tests::a_drill_undersize_never_hides_an_avoid_hit` folds one `DrillUndersize` and one `AvoidHit` for each of the five `FixturePart` values. It asserts six lines, each with its own move.

With the old key the test fails, and the output shows the defect:

```
"warning: undersize hole at move 3: ... - repeated on 1 more move (to 10)",
"warning: holder at move 11 violates protected 'Do not touch' item #1 (0.500 mm short of clearance)",
...
```

The shank hit at move 10 has no line of its own.

`operations::warning_fold_tests::an_undercut_lift_never_hides_an_avoid_hit` folds one `UndercutLift`, one `DrillUndersize` and one `AvoidHit` for each `FixturePart`. It asserts seven lines. With main's key `217` for `UndercutLift`, it fails.

## Gates

Head 9f1f7adb1 (main 2d98d87be merged in):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 3 steps, 0 failed (`ui build`, `ui suites: lib`, `ui suites: operations`).
- `warning_fold_tests`: 8 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run`: the diff reaches no heavy lane.

## Screenshots

The operation page with four warnings on one path: an undersize hole (move 3), a "Do not touch" hit of the shank (move 10), an undercut lift (move 12), and a "Do not touch" hit of the holder (move 14). The status banner is open. The images are on the images-only `pr-screenshots` branch of the fork, not on this branch.

- Before (main, keys 216 and 217): "2 warnings". The undersize line holds the shank hit as "repeated on 1 more move (to 10)". The undercut line holds the holder hit as "(to 14)". The two "Do not touch" hits have no line.
- After (this PR, keys 223 and 222): "4 warnings". Each "Do not touch" hit has its own line.

title: feat(2d): import SVG drawings as 2D sketch profiles
body:
## What changed

- A new SVG reader, `camcraft_geometry::svg`, reads an SVG file into the same `dxf::Document` as the DXF reader. The sketch chaining, nesting, `SketchData`, the `Sketch` entity and the project file are shared and do not change.
  - Elements: `path` (M L H V C S Q T A Z, absolute and relative), `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `rect` (with rx/ry), `circle`, `ellipse`.
  - Groups: `g` with `transform` (matrix, translate, scale, rotate, skewX, skewY). A `use` of an element in the same file is drawn.
  - Curves: an arc or circle that maps to a circle stays an analytic arc. Beziers and true ellipses become lines within 0.005 mm.
  - Units: `width` and `height` in mm, cm, in, pt, pc or px (96 px to the inch), with the `viewBox` and `preserveAspectRatio`.
  - Y is flipped about the page height, so the drawing looks as it does in the editor.
  - A top-level `g` is a layer (`inkscape:label`, else `id`).
  - Text, images, nested `svg`, `style`, clip paths, masks, hidden content and `use` of other files are skipped and counted by kind.
- A new undoable command, `ImportSvg` (`commands/import_svg.rs`). It wraps `ImportDxf`, so apply and invert are the same code.
- A new MCP tool, `import_svg` (`mcp/svg_tools.rs`), and a new script verb, `cam.importSvg`. They take the options of `import_dxf`.
- The user guide (units and coordinates) and the MCP tool table list SVG.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1880-svg-import.md`.

## Refusals (by name, never a panic)

- A file that states no physical size, until the caller gives the unit of one drawing unit. The size is never guessed. A unitless `width` counts as no physical size.
- A caller unit for a file that states its size (two sizes would disagree).
- Malformed XML, malformed path data, an unknown transform or a singular one.
- A zero or negative document size or viewBox. A negative shape size.
- A degenerate arc (a zero radius).
- Percent or font-relative lengths in shapes.
- A file over the import budget (bytes, elements, segments), nesting deeper than 256, and `use` chains deeper than 16 (a reference loop).
- A compressed `.svgz` file, and a file that is not UTF-8.

## Tests

- `crates/geometry/tests/svg.rs` (9 tests): a rectangle with a hole in mm (nesting, Y flip), in and pt and px and cm documents, no physical size, absolute and relative path forms, Beziers and arcs, nested group transforms and a sheared ellipse, a rounded rect with polyline and skipped content, merged short segments, compact path syntax.
- `crates/geometry/tests/svg_refusals.rs` (5 tests): malformed documents and paths, zero or negative sizes, the import budget, and a deterministic smoke fuzz (truncations and 1000 byte mutations).
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_svg.rs` (2 tests): `import_svg` end to end (units, layers, chains, skipped notes, bounds, move, undo and redo, a 2D Contour on the profile, save and reopen, the script verb), and the command's refusals and undo step.
- Red before the fix: the pins did not compile on unchanged code (`unresolved import camcraft_geometry::svg`).
- Mutation checks. Each guard was removed, the pin went red, and then the guard was restored:
  - Y flip: red (4 tests).
  - Arcs stay analytic: red (4 tests).
  - Caller unit on a sized file is refused: red.
  - A unitless size is no physical size: red.
  - Zero-radius arc refusal: red.
  - `use` depth guard: red (stack overflow).
  - Short-segment merge: red.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean (exit 0).
- Touched suites, all green:
  - geometry: `svg` 9, `svg_refusals` 5, `dxf`, `dxf_refusals`, `sketch_data`, `sketch_chains`, and the lib tests.
  - app: `mcp_svg` 2, `mcp_dxf` 2, `sketch_profile` 8, `sketch_project` 14, `scripting` 20 (it checks `cam.d.ts`), `mcp` 23, and the lib tests (290).
- The gate did not complete. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` falls back to the batch tier, because the diff touches `crates/geometry/src/lib.rs`. On this machine the shared sccache server stopped responding: each compile through it hung, including the jobs of other sessions. The gate sets the sccache wrapper itself, so it hung at the `post` build twice. Clippy and the suites above ran with the wrapper unset. The batch tier still needs a run: the post-merge gate, or a reviewer's `pr-test.yml` run.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- A posted G-code golden for a 2D Contour on an SVG profile. On `main`, a 2D Contour on a profile is accepted but does not generate yet: that is #1864 (PR #2716). Follow-up: #3042.
- The row for `import_svg` in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. The edit was blocked as a sensitive file in this session. A maintainer session can add it. Then that PR needs `Process change: yes`.
- No UI change: the app has no DXF profile import dialog yet, so there is no file dialog to extend.
- Nested `<svg>` viewports, CSS stylesheets, text to outlines and embedded images are out of scope (the issue says so). They are counted as skipped.

## Overlaps

- #2773 (draft, needs-rework) changes the stock check in `ImportDxf::build`. This PR does not change `build`. `ImportSvg` has its own copy of that 10-line check, so it does not get the #2773 change. If #2773 merges first, `ImportSvg` must get the same change.
- #2924 adds rows to `commands/mod.rs` and `script/mod.rs`, and changes `mcp/sketch_tools.rs`. This PR adds other rows to the two `mod.rs` files and puts its MCP tool in a new file. The files are the same and the functions are different. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2678 adds lines to `commands/mod.rs`. The lines are different.

Changelog: Import SVG drawings (paths, shapes, group transforms, mm/cm/in/pt/pc/px sizes) as 2D profiles on the stock, with the `import_svg` MCP tool and `cam.importSvg`; an SVG with no physical size is refused until you state its unit.

Effort: high

Fixes #1880

title: feat(ui): place DXF profiles on the stock from the Stock page and a drop
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the UI for DXF profiles over the #1862 commands (`ImportDxf`, `MoveSketch`, `DeleteEntity`). It follows the maintainer's scope change on the issue: the DXF door is on the Stock page, not on `Model > Open`.

- The Stock page has a new group "DXF profiles". It has the control "Add DXF profile…" (a `.dxf` file picker). The control is disabled when the active setup has no stock.
- The group lists each profile of the active setup with these controls:
  - "Profile X", "Profile Y" and "Profile angle (deg)". These are a draft. "Place profile" queues one `MoveSketch`.
  - "Hide profile" / "Show profile". This is view state, the same list as the browser eye.
  - "Delete profile". This queues one `DeleteEntity`.
- A `.dxf` file dropped on the viewport goes through the same import path. With no stock, the drop is refused by name: "drop refused: <file> is a DXF profile - make a stock first ...".
- A drawing without `$INSUNITS` opens the modal "DXF units". The modal shows the drawing size read in millimeters and read in inches, each with the size in the other unit. "Millimeters" or "Inches" runs `ImportDxf` with that unit. "Cancel", Escape or a backdrop click places nothing. The unit is never guessed.
- The status line shows the import summary: the name, the setup, the unit and its source (file or chosen), the layer count, the closed and open chain counts, the chains not chained, and the skipped entities by type.
- The browser shows each profile as a child row of its setup's Stock row (`Leaf::Sketch`), with the suffix "DXF profile" and the eye. A click opens the Stock page and selects the profile, so Del deletes it through the history.
- The viewport draws the profile lines, arcs and circles of the active setup on the stock top, at `sketch::world_pose`. Each free end of an open chain gets a magenta X. No curve uses that colour, so an open gap does not look closed.
- The overlay lines are cached by the sketch data `Arc` and the pose (`SketchLineCache` on `FrameCache`). A still frame builds nothing (crates/ui/AGENTS.md, frame cost).
- The operation page Source list offers the profiles of the operation's setup for a kind that `sketch_model::admits` (2D milling, plasma, wire EDM). A setup with a stock, a profile and no model can so have an operation on the profile.
- `camcraft_app` re-exports `camcraft_geometry::dxf`, so the UI can name the `Primitive` variants. This adds no crate dependency.

The import does not use `finish_import`. That function handles the model worker. `ImportDxf` checks the drawing at construction, so the typed `DxfUnitsMissing` error is caught where the UI builds the command. `docs/decisions/1863-dxf-stock-ui.md` records this and the other choices.

## Cause

The #1862 commands had no UI door. A user could place a DXF profile only through MCP or the script.

## Tests

New pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/dxf_profile.rs`:

- `the_stock_page_adds_lists_places_and_deletes_a_dxf_profile`
- `a_drawing_without_units_asks_millimeters_or_inches_and_never_guesses`
- `a_dropped_dxf_lands_on_the_stock_or_asks_for_one`
- `the_browser_lists_the_profile_under_its_stock_with_an_eye`
- `the_viewport_draws_the_chains_on_the_stock_top_and_marks_open_ends`
- `the_operation_page_takes_the_profile_as_its_source_without_a_model`
- `a_still_frame_builds_no_profile_lines_and_a_move_builds_once`

Also:

- `page_layout_windows::layout_window_dxf_units` (the named layout test of the new modal).
- `dxf_units_dialog::tests::readings_state_both_units_both_ways`.
- `dxf_drop::tests::dxf_by_extension_in_any_case`.

Red before the fix: yes. On upstream/main the pins do not compile. `CommandKind::ImportDxf`, `CommandKind::MoveSketch`, `State::dxf_units_prompt`, `Leaf::Sketch`, `sketch_overlay` and `op_source` do not exist.

Mutation checks (each red with the mutation, green when restored):

- Guess millimeters for a drawing without units: `a_drawing_without_units...` is red ("nothing lands before the answer").
- Remove the stock check of the drop: `a_dropped_dxf...` is red (the refusal does not name the file).
- Remove the profiles from the Source list: `the_operation_page...` is red.
- Draw a hidden profile: `the_viewport_draws...` is red.
- Bypass the line cache: `a_still_frame_builds...` is red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on 4cf20695e (19 steps, 0 failed: app lib, ui lib and 17 ui suites). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

## Not exercised

- The native file picker of "Add DXF profile…" is not driven in a test. The test calls the same `CommandKind::ImportDxf`.

## Overlaps

These open PRs touch the same files, in different functions. The PR that merges second refreshes.

- `crates/ui/src/state.rs`: #2999, #2993, #2992, #2981, #2979, #2978, #2974, #2972, #2969, #2968, #2964, #2955, #2951, #2786, #2773, #2763, #2932. This PR adds enum variants, two fields and four dispatch arms only.

Changelog: The Stock page places a DXF profile on the stock top ("Add DXF profile…", or drop a `.dxf` on the viewport), asks for the unit when the drawing states none, lists and places profiles, shows them in the browser and on the stock with open chain ends marked, and offers them as the Source of 2D, plasma and wire EDM operations.

title: feat(wire): post a native Agie Classic Cut 2S job
body:
**This first writer now uses the zero-step encoder from #3104. The machine template and standalone encoder have merged. The contributor has addressed the desktop review comments. A maintainer re-check is pending.** Later feature drafts still need their own safety review before they can introduce machining behavior. A stale controller quality can change the effective finish, pass count and offsets.

This change builds on the machine template in #2948 and the standalone encoder in #3104. These branches are in a fork, so this PR targets upstream main. Review [the first-writer safety adoption above its integration parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/1ea87ebac0204f3613c3d2549692b4108f620f66...025ed4760e592c3401859a66285457021a98341b).

## Change

The desktop Post command and cam.post write a native Agie job directory with linked ISO, SBR and SBL files. CamCraft writes the nominal contour in Rust. The setup requests a resident quality and leaves every work with zero erosion steps. The post validates the work before it creates the destination. It publishes all three files together and preserves an existing directory.

The supported case is one vertical rectangular punch in 20 mm stock. Select the Classic 2S template from #2948. Enter the AGIE_QN2 condition for Berco Cut 0.25 mm wire and cold die steel. Select the 1.0 mm separation cut explicitly. The template starts without an installed condition. A cut needs 0.4 mm clearance at each stock face and 3 mm of straight face on each side of the entry. Other contours, tapers, skims, custom X/Y travel limits and additional workpieces are refused.

## Reference material for review

The contributor's team wrote [Agie-CAM at 11b1bb9](https://github.com/qsmits/Agie-CAM/tree/11b1bb9ef2c752b94b6fefc1f0814acd2e030c42) and released it under the MIT license. This draft retains the license and copyright notice. The implementation reference documents observed controller examples for parts of the JEScript sequence and the resident technology selection. The published guides linked on #2945 give the file roles and some interface arguments. They do not document the full sequence and all defaults. Please review that source against the project rules before merge.

The controller supplies its own runtime and technology table. This PR includes the writer and original synthetic examples and expected output. It includes no controller image, vendor post, runtime library or technology database.

## Control verification

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Adaptive from the previous operations
body:
Stacked on #2822 (merge #2822 first).

This PR is a `feat`: it adds a parameter group. The default (off) does not change an output.

## What changed

The 2D Adaptive operation has the rest machining group.
With the group on, the operation cuts only what the earlier operations of the same setup left.

- `OpParams::Adaptive2D` has the field `rest: Option<RestParams>`. `None` is off and is the default.
- `machining2d::rest_adaptive_previous` (new, motion crate) reads the stock of the previous operations with `rest_stock_from_columns` (#2033). It gives that stock to the rest Adaptive planner `rest_adaptive` (#2031).
- Each plunge stands where that stock proves the whole cutter clear. The planner holds the optimal load on the material that stands.
- `adaptive::rest_levels` (new) gives the cut depths of the rest planner. The stock is read at exactly those depths.
- The group rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest` of the 2D Adaptive and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter. A file without the key reads as off.
- The stamp writes byte `0xD9` and the allowance when the group is on. An operation without the group keeps its stamp.

Refused by name, at the edit and again at generation:

- An entered previous tool (`REST_ADAPTIVE_ENTERED`). An entered diameter does not prove where material is absent (#2031). The 2D Pocket keeps that mode.
- The Trochoidal method, arc turns, a tilt. The rest planner does not read them, so they are not dropped silently.
- A negative or non-finite allowance.

Refused by name at generation:

- An earlier operation with no toolpath, a stale toolpath, or a suppressed cut (the refusals of #2033).
- No stock ahead (`REST_ADAPTIVE_NO_STOCK`). The 2D Pocket cuts the whole pocket in this case. The 2D Adaptive does not, because the rest planner cannot enter a full pocket.
- A roughing pass that stops above the floor: "rest Adaptive has no entry with proved clearance".

## Cause

The rest Adaptive planner (#2031) had no door from an operation.
The retired Adaptive strategy of the 2D Pocket was its only possible caller (#2253).
The 2D Adaptive operation had no rest parameter and no producer of the proved stock.

## Two findings

- The column reading of #2033 leaves a band along each wall that an earlier tool cut to. On a 0.1 mm grid the band is 0.14 mm thick. With the film of #2033 (one cell diagonal) the planner read the band as rest material and refused the fixture ("would reach 23 passes by a retract"). The film is now `cell * (1 + sqrt 2)`. The band still stands for each plunge and each load reading. No pass is planned for it. The path note states the film.
- An allowance of 0.6 mm grew that band to 0.74 mm, and the planner found no entry. The allowance now grows only material that is thicker than the film. It never makes the standing material smaller.

## Tests

Red before the change: the pins use the new field and the new function, so they do not compile on unchanged code. The mutation results are the proof for each guard.

Pins, all new:

- `crates/app/tests/rest_adaptive_op.rs` (6 tests):
  - `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left`: the real job (60 x 40 pocket, 3 mm corners, 12 mm roughing tool, 4 mm rest tool) against an independent simulation of the roughing pass. Each standing column is cut. No plunge goes down a column that the roughing pass left under the cutter. No rapid is below the top of the stock, but a straight lift. Each feed stays at a corner.
  - `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_is_refused_by_name`
  - `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit`
  - `a_document_past_the_door_is_refused_at_generation`
  - `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_a_project_file_key_and_moves_the_stamp`
  - `mcp_sets_the_group_refuses_the_entered_tool_undoes_and_the_project_keeps_it`
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`, `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool`.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_adaptive_tests.rs` (lib): `each_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `the_allowance_never_makes_the_standing_material_smaller`, `bad_rest_values_are_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs`: `the_column_stock_of_the_previous_operations_plans_the_rest_adaptive_pass` (the laws of #2031 on the column stock: verifier, plunges, rapids, load, coverage), `the_previous_operations_planner_refuses_what_it_cannot_prove`.

title: feat(2d): arc turns and their radius on Face, 2D Contour and Slot
body:
## What changed

Face, 2D Contour and Slot have the arc turns option with a corner arc radius. The parameters are `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`, the same as on 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset (#1733).

All three kinds can round their corners safely. No kind is left out.

- **2D Contour** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the tool radius, as before.
- **Face** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the semicircle of half the row spacing, as before. A smaller radius gives two quarter arcs with a straight step between them. The step is one radius outside the overrun line, away from the footprint. With a radius, rows spaced wider than the tool diameter turn on arcs too.
- **Slot** gets `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`. Each row-end corner of the serpentine pass turns on one tangent arc. No radius is the tool radius. The new module is `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_turns.rs`.

The parameter door (`sane.rs`) refuses a radius below 0.01 mm on the three kinds. The generators refuse a radius larger than the tool radius, with the text of `corner_arc_radius`. The project file writes the keys only when they are set. The cache digest reads the radius only when the option is on.

The operation pages show the radius rows when the option is on. The Face page names its default "Arc radius = half the row spacing".

MCP: `edit_operation` sets the two fields through `EditOperationParams`. No new command and no new tool are necessary.

The type is `feat`, because the change adds parameters. The task template gave `fix`.

## Cause

The fix for #1733 gave the radius to the three pocket kinds only. Face and 2D Contour had the option without a radius. Slot did not have the option.

## Which corners turn, and why no arc cuts past the wall

- 2D Contour: only a corner that turns toward the air gets an arc. This is the law of `fillet.rs`, and it did not change. A corner that turns toward the part stays sharp, and the notes name it. A convex outside corner is such a corner, so an arc cannot leave material there.
- Face: each point of a turn is on or outside the overrun line, one tool radius from the footprint. The turn reaches one radius past that line at most.
- Slot: the pass is in the cutter-center stadium, which is convex. A fillet is inside the triangle of its corner and its two tangent points, and that triangle is inside the stadium. `fillet_corners` proves each triangle again and keeps a corner sharp if it cannot prove it. An arc leaves corner rest at the round end of the slot. The note states the largest rest.

### Review fix: the Face radius bound

`corner_turn` in `blend.rs` gave the semicircle when half the row spacing was less than 0.005 mm past the radius. That semicircle is larger than the radius. Now:

- If half the spacing is not more than the radius (1e-9 mm float margin), the turn is the semicircle, as before. Its radius is not larger than the requested radius.
- If half the spacing is more than the radius by 0.005 mm or less, the turn uses two corner arcs. Their radius is half the spacing minus 0.005 mm, which is less than the requested radius. The straight step stays 0.01 mm.
- If that radius is below 0.01 mm, the turn stays sharp. The status line counts it as the `Tiny` refusal ("row spacing below the 0.020 mm arc resolution").

- Current main adds the same missing Face default in `first_traverse_mill_turn` and `model_fidelity_wide`. These literals have `blend_radius: None` too.

- The test helper in `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` also has `blend_radius: None`. Its pin is `operation::first_traverse::tests::a_mill_turn_judges_its_milling_kinds_in_the_mill_order`.

- The Contour literal in `crates/app/tests/equal_steps.rs` has `blend_radius: None`. Its pin is `equal_steps::edit_sets_equal_steps_and_undo_restores_the_remainder_ladder`.

The fix adds 18 default-field lines in fourteen files. All changed literals are in tests. It changes no runtime source logic.
